Rust is a byproduct of oxidation on ferrous metal and is harmful but can be utilized for added value.
The study utilized rust from corroded ferrous metal in Surabaya, Malang, and Bangkalan.
Rust powders were separated using a 0.1 T hard magnet.
XRF, XRD, and VSM were used for characterization.
The rust powder samples were identified as ferrites, specifically magnetite (Fe₃O₄).
The magnetite phase was confirmed by XRD with PDF codes #96-901-3530 and #96-900-5814.
The rust powder samples showed soft magnetic properties with a saturation magnetization (Ms) of 8 emu/g.
The maximum reflection loss values for the samples were -20.15 dB (Surabaya), -12.64 dB (Malang), and -6.75 dB (Bangkalan).
The reflection loss values were measured at a matching frequency of 11 GHz and a bandwidth of 3 GHz.
A reflection loss value of -20.15 dB indicates approximately 99% absorption of incident microwave energy.
The extraction process purifies the sample by removing non-magnetic impurities, enhancing microwave absorption.
The VNA was used to measure the reflection loss values of the rust powder samples.
The rust-based microwave absorbers can be used in wireless data communication and radar systems.
The study highlights the potential of using corrosion products as radar absorber materials.
The rust powder samples were found to have a high Fe content (82.63 wt%) with minor impurities such as Si, Al, Ca, Ni, etc.
The rust powder samples showed amorphous properties with low density and high porosity.
The magnetic properties of the rust powder samples were characterized as soft magnets with a coercivity field (Hc) of 0.0504 T.
The remanent magnetization (Mr) of the rust powder samples was 4.535 emu/g.
The rust powder samples were tested for microwave absorption in the X-band frequency range (8-12 GHz).
The absorption of microwaves was highest in the samples subjected to separation treatment.
The study demonstrates the feasibility of using natural ferrites from corrosion products as effective radar absorber materials.
